Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Summit Utilities Group Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. If you would like to register for a question, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Summit Utilities Group's Q3 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are John Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Reynolds, Chief Financial Officer; and Lisa Chen, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to John Thompson.

John Thompson: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by strong operational performance in our generation fleet, continued growth in our renewable energy portfolio, effective cost management, and progress on our infrastructure investments.

Let me provide some more detail on these four key aspects, starting with our strong operational performance. As a diversified utility with a 25 GW fleet spanning natural gas, nuclear, renewables, and emerging storage across PJM, ERCOT, and MISO markets, we delivered robust results despite volatile commodity prices and regulatory shifts. Financially, we exceeded expectations with consolidated revenues of $2.85 billion, up 8% year-over-year and above our guidance, powered by higher realized power prices in merchant exposures and strong contracted dispatch. Adjusted EBITDA reached $925 million, a 12% increase, with margins at 32.5%, our best Q2 since 2021—though we're building on that momentum into Q3. This came from a 15% rise in nuclear contributions, with capacity factors at 93.2% thanks to outage optimizations at key units. Diluted EPS was $1.42, beating consensus, aided by O&M costs at $285 per MWh, down 4%.

Operationally, generation hit 28.2 TWh, up 7%, with thermal fleet heat rates at 7,650 Btu/kWh from turbine upgrades on our 2.2 GW Panda plants in Texas. Renewables produced 3.8 TWh from our 4.5 GW portfolio, up 22%, boosted by wind at 38% capacity factors and the full ramp of our 300 MW Desert Sun solar-plus-storage in ERCOT, with 150 MWh batteries at 95% availability under a 15-year PPA. Strategically, we closed a $1.2 billion acquisition of 800 MW wind assets in PJM, pushing renewables to 28% of capacity toward our 40% by 2030 goal, with repowering for 15% output gains. Our CCUS pilot at Limestone captured 90% CO2 over 500 hours, eyeing $50 million in 45Q credits, and we deployed 50 MW NexusFlow batteries at 98% efficiency for ancillary revenue.

In ERCOT, Texas demand grew 5% from data centers, dispatching gas at 85% with $85/MWh peaks. PJM capacity awards secured 95% at premiums for $450 million forward revenue, and MISO hydro hit 42% factors. Capex was $650 million, 60% to renewables and storage, generating $550 million free cash flow for returns. Challenges included low gas at $2.85/MMBtu, shaving $75 million EBITDA despite 70% hedges; coal costs up 6% idling 200 MW; FERC delays pushing solar to 2026; Texas winterization O&M; droughts cutting hydro; curtailments; supply chain hikes on modules to $0.32/W; labor inflation; and softer wholesale at $42/MWh. Our diversification, AI dispatch saving 2% fuel, and hedging keep us resilient, reaffirming full-year EBITDA guidance with Q3 strength from nuclear and peaks.

Next, our continued growth in the renewable energy portfolio ties directly to rate base expansion, a cornerstone of our earnings trajectory. Our consolidated rate base ended Q2 at $28.4 billion, up 7.2% year-over-year and 3.8% sequentially—outpacing the 5-6% industry average. Trailing 12-month AFUDC added $142 million, up 15%, from construction at a 7.2% cost of capital. Capex of $1.7 billion YTD is on track for $3.8-4.0 billion, 60% above depreciation. T&D took 55% at $935 million, like the $450 million 345 kV Huntley-Evergreen line adding 1,200 MW in PJM and HTLS reconductoring in MISO South for 8-10% load growth. Generation and storage got 30% at $510 million, including 450 MW solar like SolarPeak in Georgia with 30% ITC and CWIP at 10.2% ROE, plus 200 MW/800 MWh Liberty BESS in Ohio for MISO ancillaries. Grid mod 15% covered AMI and DERMS for 12% rooftop solar.

Midwest (45% of rate base) grew 8.1% on formula rates; Southeast 6.9% post-hurricanes; West 9.2% on wildfire upgrades. Headwinds: 12% steel/transformer costs, rates compressing equity, regulatory lag on Georgia case. Levers for 6-8% growth: 15% peak demand from data centers/EVs justifying $12 billion T&D; IRA $450 million credits; $2-3 billion M&A from 5 GW queue. Q3 sequential growth 2.0%, supporting EPS guidance.

On effective cost management, this has enabled our sustainable dividend policy and payout strategy, a pillar of capital allocation. Serving 4.2 million customers in PJM and MISO with a $28 billion regulated rate base and 3.2 GW unregulated renewables—including SunForge solar and Eagle Wind—we've paid dividends 52 years straight. Quarterly dividend $0.62/share, annualized $2.48, yielding 4.2% versus Duke's 4.1%, Southern's 3.8%. We target 65-75% payout of adjusted earnings; trailing EPS $3.52 puts us at 70.4%, up from 68.2%, with 6.8% growth. Covered 1.9x by op cash, 1.7x FCF, beating S&P average.

This band balances returns and reinvestment amid regulated ROEs at 9.8%, PPAs with Google/Amazon, stress-tested to hold above 60% in shocks, backed by A- rating and $1.2 billion cash. Five-year 5.2% CAGR beats sector 4.1%, tied to 4-6% EPS from 6-8% rate base. Q3's 12th stable quarter despite $2.1 billion capex up 12% for grid hardening and DERs. 2025 payout to 72-75% on 7.2% EPS from $1.8 billion rate wins like Pennsylvania EV rider. Electrification (2.5% demand growth, 15 GW data centers) justifies $4.5 billion capex—40% transmission, 30% renewables/BESS like IronPeak. Below 65%, buybacks ($250 million YTD); above 75%, deferrals. MISO steady at 68%; PJM renewables at 25% (40% by 2028) via green bonds, $180 million tax equity. AI model simulates scenarios with hedges at $3.20 gas; debt at 4.9%, cost 6.2%. Dynamic corridors on FFO/debt 20.1%. Total yield 7-9%, Dividend Aristocrat path, $10k to $28.4k over 10 years.

Finally, progress on infrastructure investments shapes our forward-looking outlook. As noted earlier, our statements are safe-harbored, subject to risks like weather, supply chains, FERC, NERC in SEC filings. We guide 7-9% annual EPS growth through 2028, from data centers, onshoring, decarbonization; U.S. demand 2.5-3% CAGR, our territories leading. EBITDA 8-10% to $4.2-4.4 billion in 2025 at 42-44% margins, 85% capacity locked, renewables/storage 35% with $25-30/MWh LCOE versus gas $35. Target 55% carbon-free by 2030, ROE 10.5-11%.

Capex $11-13 billion five-year, up 15%: 50% renewables/BESS ($5.5-6.5B) like 2.5 GW ERCOT solar-BESS COD 2027-28 at 12% IRR with Ørsted; 30% grid ($3.3-3.9B); 20% nuclear/CCUS ($2.2-2.6B) with PJM $1.2B hydrogen peakers $150-180/kW-year, MISO 1.2 GWh batteries. Texas +4% loads; PJM black-start from Comanche uprate. VPPs aggregate 500 MW DERs; Blue Hydrogen 200 MW with Exxon for 45Q. Stress-tested leverage 3.5-4.0x, top-quartile availability. $50B TAM, 60-70% payouts, $1.5B FCF post-2026.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael to discuss the financials.

Michael Reynolds: Thank you, John. Good morning, everyone. For the Q3, we reported adjusted earnings per share of $0.90 and revenue of $2.90 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Our capital expenditure for the quarter was $675 million, primarily focused on renewables expansion and transmission upgrades. We remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning value to shareholders.

John Thompson: Thank you, Michael. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your plans for dividend increases amid higher capex?

John Thompson: Certainly. Our policy is built for growth at 5% CAGR, linked to EPS expansion, with coverage metrics like 1.7x FCF providing ample room. We're positioned for a hike next February, supported by rate wins and cash generation, targeting the upper payout band without compromising reinvestment.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: What is your outlook for rate base growth into 2025?

Michael Reynolds: We see sustained 6-8% annual growth, driven by $3.8-4 billion capex, electrification tailwinds adding 15% to peaks, IRA credits, and our 5 GW queue. Q4 should deliver another 2% sequential, setting up strong 2025 earnings.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Lee: How are you mitigating risks related to supply chain disruptions in renewables?

Lisa Chen: We're de-risking through domestic partnerships like First Solar, long-lead hedging for transformers, and a robust queue with PPAs—80% fixed-rate financing locked. Diversification across ERCOT/PJM/MISO and tech like HTLS conductors keeps us ahead of bottlenecks.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to John Thompson for closing remarks.

John Thompson: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in the Q3, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning Summit Utilities Group for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in Summit Utilities Group.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
